A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DEER research, despite the revised title. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original NER experiments across five datasets and four LLMs, together with retrieval ablations, low-resource experiments, and appendix error analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds a retrieval-quality analysis and further reported baseline comparisons.

M1.justification: DEER retains the same label statistics, weighted token-matching and embedding retrieval, and sequential unseen-token, false-negative, and boundary reflection. Splitting data preparation into Section 2.2 changes exposition, not the procedure; the appendix prompts are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate NCBI, bc2gm, CoNLL03, OntoNotes, and TweetNER7, retaining the same domains, flat-NER task, seen/unseen analyses, and low-resource coverage. The added retrieval diagnostic uses existing data rather than introducing a new task or environment.

E2.justification: Table 4 expands the supervised comparisons from BERT-base and UniversalNER-7B to also include InstructUIE-11B and GoLLIE-13B/34B. New appendix Table 14 directly compares GPT-NER with DEER across three LLMs. These substantive additions broaden comparison with specialized models and the closely related entity-based retriever; their earlier citations alone did not constitute these comparisons.

E3.justification: New Table 6 introduces a retrieval-quality evaluation measuring the proportion of entities shared by training and test data that occur in eight retrieved demonstrations. Existing mention-level evaluation, test-set sampling, demonstration budgets, and training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.1 adds a sanity check testing whether label-guided retrieval supplies demonstrations containing relevant known entities. Existing context-length, token-weight, embedding, prompting-format, low-resource, output-failure, and error-breakdown analyses are retained, including in the appendices.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging BERT results over three random seeds and estimating 95% confidence intervals with 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Appendix A.2 and the reported margins of error are unchanged; no new uncertainty-reporting procedure accompanies the added comparisons.

E6.justification: Most existing results remain unchanged, with supporting results added in Tables 4, 6, and 14. Table 6 reports OntoNotes retrieval coverage of 62.7 for sentence retrieval versus 80.6 for DEER; Table 14 shows a GPT-4o tie at 82.7. Table 2 changes GPT-4o-mini NCBI scores from 77.6 to 77.3 without reflection and 80.3 to 79.3 with reflection under unchanged reported settings. The displayed averages remain 74.1 and 75.8, although the revised rows imply 74.0 and 75.6.

T1.justification: The token and span definitions, retrieval equations (1)–(5), and error ontology retain their mathematical substance. The new retrieval diagnostic introduces an empirical measure, without adding formal theory, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction strengthens the thesis from inefficient use of training labels to the claim that the performance gap primarily reflects retrieval inefficiency rather than inherent LLM limitations. The central DEER contributions and claims of competitiveness with supervised models, unseen-entity effectiveness, and low-resource robustness were already present in v1.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 interprets the new entity-coverage diagnostic as validating the criticism of generic retrievers. Section 4 broadens its comparison language from matching BERT and narrowing the UniNER gap to comparable or superior performance against five fine-tuned baselines. The stated limitations and appendix explanations of failure conditions are retained.

D1.justification: v2 newly identifies the API models as gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 and gpt-4o-2024-08-06 in Section 3.3, footnote 5. This improves documentation without establishing a model change. Prompts, DEER and BERT hyperparameters, and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The expanded baseline descriptions add Chung et al. (2022) on instruction-finetuned models and Rozière et al. (2024) on Code Llama. InstructUIE, GoLLIE, and GPT-NER were already cited in v1. The related-work structure and principal training-free positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds the title prefix 'LLMs are Better Than You Think,' rewrites the abstract and selected introduction and conclusion passages, and separates problem setup from data-statistics preparation. Baseline descriptions expand, but most methodological exposition and appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the retrieval-quality and GPT-NER tables, expands Table 4 with three comparator columns, and revises Figure 2's stage labels and styling. Captions and placement change locally; the other figures and existing appendix displays are retained with renumbering and reflow.

improvement.justification: The broader comparisons, direct retrieval diagnostic, and exact API identifiers modestly improve empirical support and reproducibility. These gains are limited by new reporting inconsistencies: revised Table 2 scores leave stale averages and disagree with retained appendix values, while Table 14 claims consistent outperformance despite an 82.7 tie. The additions improve assessment of the unchanged method, but the unresolved inconsistencies and stronger retrieval-causality claim prevent a substantial quality improvement.
